# Chamber Bakeout

Any chamber that has been vented comes back with water bound to its inner walls,
and that water desorbs slowly enough to hold the sector two orders of magnitude
above its operating level for weeks. A bakeout drives it off in days instead.

The sector is wrapped in heater tapes and insulation, pumped down with a turbo
cart, and ramped at no more than 30 degrees per hour to a soak temperature the
weakest component in the sector can tolerate — usually limited by a bellows or a
ceramic feedthrough rather than by the chamber itself. Thermocouples on every
tape are logged, and the ramp aborts if any two disagree.

After a soak of typically 48 hours the sector is cooled at the same rate, the
getter strips are activated near the top of the cool-down, and the sputter-ion
pumps are switched on. A residual-gas scan taken before the tapes are removed
confirms that the water peak has collapsed and no leak signature remains.

A sector that will not reach its target after a full cycle is treated as a leak
and helium-tested rather than baked again.
